subject: Approval request: rollback-bridge policy and automated reversion for canary traffic
messages:
From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acuityhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production rollout questions — canary safety nets

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Before we go live with the A-B canary next week we need a written commitment on how Redwood will mitigate SLA exposure if the canary causes a latency spike or error rate increase. Specifically: automatic fallback triggers, how long a pinned rollback lasts, and whether you can guarantee no more than 1x SLA credit window if an autorevert occurs.

Attached are our traffic dashboards and a brief list of business-critical endpoints. Can you share an actionable policy we can sign off on (so procurement and our security team can close the loop)?

We need this finalized by EOD Tuesday to keep the kick-off.

Jamie
Ops Lead, Acuity Health
attachments: prod_traffic_dashboard.png, rollback_playbook_draft.pdf
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production rollout questions — canary safety nets

Hi Jamie — thanks for sending the dashboards. We can commit to a deterministic rollback policy that preserves your SLA while enabling the canary. High level summary below (we've kept the language actionable for procurement/security):

- Canary progression: 0% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over a 24-hour window, with manual hold points at 20% and 50%.
- Automatic reversion triggers (auto-revert):
  - p95 latency > 250ms and increase of >= 20% vs baseline sustained for 5 minutes, OR
  - error rate (5xx or invalid model outputs flagged by your validation webhook) rises by >= 3 percentage points over baseline for 10 minutes.
- Reversion action: immediate traffic shift back to the pinned stable variant + prefix KV cache flush to remove stale partial outputs.
- Pin duration and behavior: pinned variant remains primary for at least 60 minutes after an auto-revert. During that time we will run a short diagnostic run (telemetry + golden prompt smoke tests) before we attempt a re-roll.
- SLA carveout: an auto-revert event will not count as an SLA breach provided: (1) rollback occurred within the stated trigger windows; (2) the pinned variant served until the diagnostic period finished; (3) Redwood provides an incident report within 24 hours. If these conditions are met, we propose limited SLA credit (a single day pro-rated credit) as the default remediation; exceptions can be negotiated in contract amendments.
- Safety controls: canary traffic is routed to isolated GPU pool with KV cache isolation; we will enable sampling for debug traces at 100% for affected requests during the canary and auto-revert.

Request: please confirm approval of the above policy or highlight any must-have modifications. If approved, we will attach this language as an operational appendix to the SOW and trigger the DocuSign envelope.

I will also add a short runbook for your SREs to the Ops Confluence (link in follow-up).

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production rollout questions — canary safety nets

Karthik — quick internal note before we finalize wording for Acuity: two small guardrails I want added to the appendix.

1) Time-based cool-off: If an auto-revert happens twice within a 72-hour window for the same endpoint, we auto-block re-roll attempts for 7 days unless a joint postmortem approves a restart. Helps avoid flapping in high-traffic flows.
2) Cross-region swap approval: For cross-region failovers (us-east <-> us-west) require an explicit two-person approval from Redwood on-call + Acuity SRE unless the canary is <5% traffic.

If you're good with those I will append them to the SOW text. Also adding the quick diagnostic checklist we run post-revert (sample set of golden prompts, CPU/GPU perf snapshot, and a short sanity check of embeddings distribution).

-Marissa
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acuityhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production rollout questions — canary safety nets

Logan, Marissa, Karthik — thank you. This reads well and addresses our security and procurement concerns. Two confirmations from our side:

- Agree to the auto-revert thresholds and the 60-minute pin window.
- Approve the time-based cool-off and cross-region approval guardrails (good additions).

Next steps: please add the operational appendix to the SOW and send the DocuSign envelope for the amendment (Deal ID ACU-2026-0891). We will countersign once our legal has a quick look (should be fine).

Jamie
Ops Lead, Acuity Health
